name: Plastic Bottle
description: A common plastic drink bottle used for water and soft drinks.
reuse: Reuse it as a small storage container or for simple craft projects.
repair: Plastic bottles are generally not suitable for repair.
recycle: Empty and rinse the bottle before placing it in the recycling bin.
dispose: If it cannot be recycled, place it in the general waste bin.

name: Cardboard Box
description: Cardboard packaging commonly used for deliveries and storage.
reuse: Reuse the box for storage, moving items or packaging.
repair: Small tears can be repaired using paper tape.
recycle: Flatten the box before placing it in the recycling bin.
dispose: Wet or heavily contaminated cardboard should go in general waste.

name: Glass Jar
description: A glass container commonly used for food and drinks.
reuse: Reuse the jar for food storage, organising small items or craft projects.
repair: Broken or cracked glass jars should not be repaired or reused.
recycle: Empty and rinse the jar before placing it in the recycling bin.
dispose: Broken glass should be wrapped safely and placed in general waste if required.

name: Old Mobile Phone
description: An electronic device containing reusable and recyclable materials.
reuse: Donate or sell the phone if it is still working.
repair: Consider replacing the battery, screen or other damaged parts.
recycle: Take the phone to an approved e-waste recycling collection point.
dispose: Do not place mobile phones in general household waste.

name: Plastic Food Container
description: A plastic container commonly used for takeaway food or food storage.
reuse: Reuse it for storing food or organising small household items.
repair: Cracked plastic containers are generally not suitable for repair.
recycle: Clean the container and check whether your local recycling service accepts it.
dispose: If it is heavily damaged or contaminated, place it in general waste.

name: Newspaper
description: Printed paper commonly used for news and advertising.
reuse: Reuse newspaper for wrapping, cleaning windows or craft projects.
repair: Newspaper does not normally require repair.
recycle: Place clean and dry newspaper in the paper recycling bin.
dispose: Wet or heavily contaminated newspaper should go in general waste.

name: Glass Bottle
description: A glass bottle commonly used for drinks and food products.
reuse: Reuse it for storage, decoration or craft projects if it is undamaged.
repair: Cracked or broken glass bottles should not be repaired.
recycle: Empty and rinse the bottle before recycling.
dispose: Broken glass should be wrapped safely before placing it in general waste if required.

name: Old Laptop
description: A portable computer containing electronic components and recyclable materials.
reuse: Donate or sell the laptop if it is still working.
repair: Consider replacing the battery, storage drive, keyboard or screen.
recycle: Take it to an approved e-waste recycling facility.
dispose: Do not place laptops in household general waste.

name: Plastic Shopping Bag
description: A lightweight plastic bag commonly used for carrying shopping.
reuse: Reuse it as a bin liner, storage bag or shopping bag.
repair: Small tears may be repaired with tape for temporary reuse.
recycle: Take soft plastics to a suitable collection point if one is available.
dispose: Place it in general waste if no recycling option is available.

name: Cereal Box
description: A lightweight cardboard box commonly used for packaged cereal.
reuse: Reuse it for crafts, storage or organising documents.
repair: Small tears can be repaired with paper tape.
recycle: Flatten the box and place it in the paper recycling bin.
dispose: Heavily contaminated cardboard should go in general waste.
